readme.head:
# Farfalle

Open-source AI-powered search engine. (Perplexity Clone)

Run local LLMs (**llama3**, **gemma**, **mistral**, **phi3**), custom LLMs through **LiteLLM**, or use cloud models (**Groq/Llama3**, **OpenAI/gpt4-o**)

https://github.com/rashadphz/farfalle/assets/20783686/9527a8c9-a13b-4e53-9cda-a3ab28d671b2

Please feel free to contact me on [Twitter](https://twitter.com/rashadphz) or [create an issue](https://github.com/rashadphz/farfalle/issues/new) if you have any questions.

## 💻 Live Demo

[farfalle.dev](https://farfalle.dev/) (Cloud models only)

## 📖 Overview

- 🛠️ [Tech Stack](#%EF%B8%8F-tech-stack)
- 🏃🏿‍♂️ [Getting Started](#%EF%B8%8F-getting-started)
- 🚀 [Deploy](#-deploy)

## 🛣️ Roadmap

- [x] Add support for local LLMs through Ollama
- [x] Docker deployment setup
- [x] Add support for [searxng](https://github.com/searxng/searxng). Eliminates the need for external dependencies.
- [x] Create a pre-built Docker Image
- [x] Add support for custom LLMs through LiteLLM
- [x] Chat History
- [x] Expert Search
- [ ] Chat with local files



## 🛠️ Tech Stack

- Frontend: [Next.js](https://nextjs.org/)
- Backend: [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/)
- Search API: [SearXNG](https://github.com/searxng/searxng), [Tavily](https://tavily.com/), [Serper](https://serper.dev/), [Bing](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/bing/apis/bing-web-search-api)
- Logging: [Logfire](https://pydantic.dev/logfire)
- Rate Limiting: [Redis](https://redis.io/)
- Components: [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/)


## Features
- Search with multiple search providers (Tavily, Searxng, Serper, Bing)
- Answer questions with cloud models (OpenAI/gpt4-o, OpenAI/gpt3.5-turbo, Groq/Llama3)
- Answer questions with local models (llama3, mistral, gemma, phi3)
- Answer questions with any custom LLMs through [LiteLLM](https://litellm.vercel.app/docs/providers)
- Search with an agent that plans and executes the search for better results

## 🏃🏿‍♂️ Getting Started Locally

### Prerequisites

- [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/)
- [Ollama](https://ollama.com/download) (If running local models)
  - Download any of the supported models: **llama3**, **mistral**, **gemma**, **phi3**
  - Start ollama server `ollama serve`

### Get API Keys

- [Tavily (Optional)](https://app.tavily.com/home)
- [Serper (Optional)](https://serper.dev/dashboard)
- [OpenAI (Optional)](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys)
- [Bing (Optional)](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/bing/apis/bing-web-search-api)
- [Groq (Optional)](https://console.groq.com/keys)

### Quick Start:
```
git clone https://github.com/rashadphz/farfalle.git
cd farfalle && cp .env-template .env
```
Modify .env with your API keys (Optional, not required if using Ollama)

Start the app:
```
docker-compose -f docker-compose.dev.yaml up -d
```

Wait for the app to start then visit [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000).

profile.one_liner: Farfalle is an open-source answer engine like Perplexity: you ask a question, it searches the web and writes a cited answer. It is for people who want to self-host it with local or cloud models.

jobs.job: Write cited answers from web results
jobs.how: Search results are put into a prompt that tells the model to answer only from them and cite with [number]. The text streams back through LiteLLM via LlamaIndex.

cited.text: Generate a comprehensive and informative answer for a given question solely based on the provided web Search Results (URL, Page Title, Summary). You must only use information from the provided search results. Use an unbiased and journalistic tone.

jobs.job: Switch between cloud, local and custom models
jobs.how: A model map sends each choice to a LiteLLM model string: OpenAI gpt-4o, Groq llama-3.1-70b, Ollama llama3.1, gemma, mistral, phi3, or a custom one set in an env var.
The model is asked for a structured query plan of up to 4 steps with dependencies, then for search queries per step. instructor validates the output into Pydantic models.

jobs.job: Rewrite follow-up questions using chat history
jobs.how: With earlier messages present, the model is prompted to turn the new question into a standalone search query.
A prompt gives the model the question and search context and asks for exactly three follow-up questions.

cited.text: Given a question and search result context, generate 3 follow-up questions the user might ask. Use the original question and context.

jobs.job: Fetch web results to ground answers
jobs.how: Pluggable search providers (SearXNG, Tavily, Serper, Bing) return text results and images, cached in Redis for two hours.

stack_lock: Backend is Python, so new Python libraries, LiteLLM-supported models and HTTP APIs can be adopted directly.
Local models run through Ollama, so new local models must be available as Ollama or GGUF builds.
Frontend is Next.js/TypeScript and only talks to the backend over HTTP and server-sent events, so AI changes mostly belong in the backend.
New search sources fit as another provider class behind the existing search interface.
Code is TypeScript and Python: only libraries in TypeScript and Python, unless they ship an MCP server or an API.
APIs, MCP servers and skills always pass.

findings.title: Add a first test set so prompt and model changes can be checked before they ship
findings.why: The product sends several prompts to many models (cloud, Ollama, custom) through one call path, and the files shown include no test set for any of it. Without cases, a model swap or prompt edit can quietly make answers worse. DeepEval fits the Python backend as pytest-style cases. promptfoo is a Node tool that runs separately and needs 20 to 50 cases written. Lets every other lever be measured. No gain number of its own.

findings.title: gpt-4o and 1 more OpenAI model shut down on 14 Jan 2027
findings.why: gpt-4o shuts down on 14 Jan 2027. Named successor: gpt-6-luna. gpt-4o-mini shuts down on 14 Jan 2027. Named successor: gpt-6-luna. Farfalle sends gpt-4o and gpt-4o-mini to OpenAI, and both are offered in its model list, so both stop working on 14 Jan 2027. Move both to gpt-6-luna, which OpenAI lists at a lower price. Unless reasoning effort is none, gpt-6-luna rejects temperature and top_p, and it supports function calling only with effort none. The pro-search planning calls use structured output, so test them first, and check answer quality on your own prompts.

held_back.thing: An MCP server for this API, with FastMCP or the official SDK
held_back.reason: Farfalle is a search app for people at a browser, with a chat endpoint that streams answers and a history endpoint, so nothing in the code shows an agent would call it, and the pattern is information only.
Farfalle fetches web results through its own pluggable search providers, so an MCP server adds no fit for the cited-answer job.

held_back.thing: Anthropic's lower prompt cache read price on Claude Sonnet 5.5
held_back.reason: The cited-answer prompt in the code is built fresh from each search's results, there is no caching setting to turn on, and no Anthropic model is offered.
LiteLLM already routes every model choice here, so a gateway would add a hop the product doesn't need.
The model map already sends each choice through LiteLLM, so another gateway layer adds nothing.
The product doesn't connect users to MCP servers, and it already switches models through LiteLLM.
It is a TypeScript package for the Vercel AI SDK, while the Python backend already calls Ollama through LiteLLM.

held_back.thing: agent-json-reliability (Python JSON repair and schema validation)
held_back.reason: instructor already validates the query plan into Pydantic models and retries, so a separate JSON repair library adds nothing here.
The listing only says it is newer and stronger at multi-step reasoning, with no concrete gain for the query plan that the page states. A newer model alone is not a reason to switch.

held_back.thing: ragleap-rag (self-hosted RAG engine with query rewriting)
held_back.reason: It is a whole retrieval engine, not a small piece. The product already rewrites follow-ups with one prompt, and adopting it would replace the search flow rather than improve that step.
They target coding agents with long sessions. Farfalle's rewrite step sends a short chat history, so there is nothing to compress.
It is a TypeScript SDK, and the follow-up question job runs in the Python backend through LiteLLM and instructor, which already handle structured output.
It would replace LiteLLM, which the Python backend already uses, with a TypeScript client that adds nothing the follow-up question job needs.
It reads privacy policies and is not a tool for generating follow-up questions on web search answers.

The search job already runs through four pluggable providers behind a common interface, and an MCP server adds a tool-calling layer this fixed search-then-answer flow doesn't use; the code has no sign it would give better results.
Perplexity's API is a competing answer engine for this Perplexity clone, so it is never a fit.
Tavily is already integrated in tavily.py, and this package is a JavaScript wrapper for another agent framework, while the search code is Python.
It is a command-line tool for terminals, not a search provider for the Python backend, and nothing in the code shows a gap it would fill.
Being behind isn't enough, and no release notes were read that name what this code would gain.

rank_explanation: Order: the biggest lever first, by (cost today - frontier cost) x assumed calls - cost of change. Then levers with no number, anything breaking within 30 days first, then the biggest proven gain per hour of work. A lever that doesn't pay back at that volume comes after those. Retired and retiring models come last.
